rows.what the ink shows: A low curved s-like stroke is followed by a separate high dot; there is no tall t stem or crossbar such as in the nearby et.
The upper integral limit has two open lower lobes with short raised ends, unlike the closed double loop in the adjacent +infinity below.
After alpha(f), the differential has a small lower-left closed d bowl, a taller loop above, and a compact crossed upright on the right; no separate sequence of m humps is visible.

The rotated margin clearly gives the c/r/o/i/s sequence, abbreviation point, then a low joined stroke and a separate dotted si. The intervening joined stroke has a small crest but does not expose a distinct f ascender or enough separate letters to resolve en f.
Beneath the crossing rules, the opening angular N and broad o loop are followed by a tall crossed t, low continuation, and final small s hook.

Upright bounding strokes and the central joined f survive. The relation has an angled upper stroke returning to a left-facing point, distinguishing it from two parallel equals strokes. Any lower relation bar lies on the long cancellation line, leaving less-than versus less-than-or-equal unresolved. The final symbol has a closed bowl with a visible lower-right exit foot, supporting a rather than zero.

A looped first f and a second tall f are visible, followed by a crossed plus. The connecting horizontal stroke merges with a cancellation rule; after the plus, several slanted uprights and a loop survive, but the supposed double norm bars cannot all be distinguished from the large crossing strokes.

The word after Soit has low initial humps, a small upright near its middle, and a final raised turn. Two long cancellation lines cover the letter bodies and leave no reliable separation of the internal letter sequence.
The character has two tall angled uprights joined by a deep central valley; it is a capital M, rather than the low rounded two-lobed omega visible in nearby interval endpoints.

Between un and the final accented cluster, a descending hooked stroke, low joins, a v-like notch and short uprights remain. Multiple horizontal and diagonal deletion strokes obscure both the letter bodies and word boundaries; no secure two-word reading survives.

The final cluster has low rounded joins and a detached diagonal accent above its right side. The doubled crossing rule passes through the bodies, and no clear l ascender or complete ree sequence can be isolated.
The deleted word begins with a tall t stem, continues through low joined bowls, then has a second short upright and terminal rightward e stroke; these survive above the deletion line.

The deleted word has a tall descending p with an upper loop, one low rounded return immediately after it and a final r-like rise. The heavy cancellation crosses the joining stroke that would distinguish a from ou.

A curved opening parenthesis and a low rounded trace after it remain visible. The tall vertical cancellation and its heavy horizontal crossing cover the final letter; the nearby small mark does not securely establish the grave accent.
After Polya the word consists of a short flattened n stroke, a detached round central o and a second low horizontal n stroke. These three visible components support non.
The right-margin word begins with an open c followed by a rounded compressed r/o group and a separate i dot. Two dark short s-like forms precede the low an connection and the final te return.

The inserted first word has an open c, a long nearly horizontal middle connection, a dark central upright/join, and two short terminal strokes. The middle letters are too contracted to distinguish condition securely.

The second inserted word shows an initial rounded d/é group with a detached mark above, a tall f stem, and two separate i dots around the low n connection, ending in a small e curve before the period.

Below the inserted continue, the cancelled word retains a dense looped opening, several repeated rising diagonal cancellation strokes and a final horizontal tail. The original letter sequence cannot be separated from the overwriting.

The capital P has a distinct detached prime at its upper right. The baseline and lower-right position where the index would occur are merged into the thick deletion; no separate two-curve 3 can be securely isolated.

The first short word is almost entirely merged into the cancellation. In the next word two tall t strokes enclose a small round o and flat u. The final word retains an initial c/o trace, long low m connection, descending p, and terminal t, supporting tout compact.

The initial capital is a tall closed D loop returning to a horizontal exit stroke, followed by a low rounded o and paired n-like valleys; the later small o/n forms and terminal s-like sweep support Donnons. The opening does not have the separate curved S and descending pp expected in Supposons.

A small separate en-like curve precedes a tall f stem with a short rightward cross stroke. The rest is a long low connecting stroke followed by two small vertically separated marks before the comma; their contracted form does not securely distinguish fait from fin.

The small raised sign has two rounded lobes joined by a central waist, securely supporting infinity rather than a single circular composition sign. The left glyph has a P-like loop, but the crossing baseline and a separate curved stroke at the far right obscure the complete canceled grouping and its attachment. The whole proposed P-with-raised-infinity group therefore remains uncertain; the extra curved trace is not silently asserted as a parenthesis.

The coefficient begins with a rounded stroke open at the upper right, followed by a low horizontal tail. The detached index dot lies to its right; there is no closed a bowl or separate right-hand a stem.

On reinspection, the deleted material has a lower right-opening e-like return and a smaller raised loop with a rightward cross-stroke resembling f. The two visible levels support e with superscript f, while no separate horizontal e-x-p sequence is present. Heavy vertical cancellation merges portions of the stems, limiting confidence; the new uncanceled f remains farther down and right.
The word has a low hooked initial s, a stretched linking middle stroke, a detached dot above the i position, and a short terminal upright with a rightward foot for t.

Inside the lower formula the coefficient has a closed oval bowl with a short rising stroke on its right and a horizontal exit; the index dot follows. This differs visibly from the open c in the upper formula.

The central f has a tall upright, cross stroke and long descending loop; curved strokes on its sides show the parentheses. The leading letter is almost entirely absorbed by two horizontal cancellation strokes, so its proposed m humps cannot be distinguished.
The inserted initial letter is a small oval attached to a short descending stem, giving lowercase p; the tall looped f and two parentheses follow. Two separate vertically placed dots form the colon.

After the preceding phi and comma, the coefficient starts with a small open curved hook extended into a low horizontal stroke. A distinct index dot sits above and to the right; there is no closed a bowl.

A short open left curve and two low dark remnants survive below the long rising cancellation line. The middle and final strokes are joined into the deletion ink, so the proposed a-r sequence cannot be read securely.

The first word starts with a low open curve, then a taller l stroke and low joined u-i strokes with the i dot above. The separated following small word has an accent stroke above its final vowel, supporting où.
The isolated letter before est consists of two adjacent shallow troughs and a high final upturn, the visible W shape; it has no round bowl or vertical stem suggesting another letter.
